prose_updates.tldr: The endpoint \(L(\mathbf P)\) is the sharp uncentered causal second moment compatible with \(K\) observed potential-outcome marginals, not a centered variance residual. On the common fixed-\(d>4\), \(K\ge3\), balanced overlap with Gao--Ge--Qian, the core proves a sharper empirical-MOT upper bound, the residual envelope \(r/K^2\), and optimal-sum diameter \(2\sqrt r\). Combining the improved term \(K^{-1}m^{-2/d}\) with an all-estimator Bernoulli converse gives matching root-\(N\) estimation bounds whenever \(K\gtrsim N^{q_d}\), where \(q_5=1/6\) and \(q_d=1/4\) for \(d\ge6\). The calibrated rule \(B_N^{\mathrm{plug}}=\max\{0,\widehat L-U_{N,K}/\alpha\}\) is uniformly honest by Markov's inequality and has matching root-\(N\) minimax expected excess length in the same region. The exact estimation and one-sided length frontiers for \(K=o(N^{q_d})\), including fixed-\(K\) logarithms, remain open. The finite-support simultaneous-marginal template is defined but not instantiated: endpoint separation, mixture indistinguishability, and reduced-cost resistance to every rematching column remain explicit targets. A rational-grid primal--dual procedure separates numerical error from sampling error. The STAR audit remains conditional on known bounded scaling, an i.i.d. superpopulation, complete randomization, and randomized balanced subsampling, and does not validate the native \(161/37/36\) plug-in calculation.

project_justification.gap: On the common fixed-\(d>4\), \(K\ge3\), \(N=Km\) overlap, Gao--Ge--Qian Theorem 1 gives the empirical term \(K^{-1/2}m^{-2/d}\), while their Proposition 2 prints a two-margin lower term involving \((m\log m)^{-2/d}\); their published class also covers all dimensions and \(K\ge2\). On the overlap, both analyses allow the same arbitrary \(\mathcal P(\mathbb B_d)^K\) marginals, and their balanced i.i.d.-unit sampling induces this note's armwise product law. Manole--Niles-Weed leave logarithmic slack already at two margins, and no located result supplies an ordered multi-margin expected-length converse or aggregate growing-tuple dual complexity.
project_justification.fill: The project proves the sharp residual and support-diameter geometry, the improved empirical upper rate, and matching root-\(N\) estimation and uniformly honest one-sided expected excess length for \(K\gtrsim N^{q_d}\), with \(q_5=1/6\) and \(q_d=1/4\) for \(d\ge6\). The honest construction is the explicit Markov-calibrated empirical-MOT plug-in lower bound. The remaining small-arm question asks whether aggregate jointly conjugate complexity improves \(K^{-1}m^{-2/d}\) or whether a matching simultaneous lower family exists. The finite-support template is defined but not instantiated: its endpoint separation, mixture indistinguishability, and resistance to every rematching column remain proof targets. Rational mesh, cost allowance, primal lifting, and dual shifting produce an auditable numerical bracket.

prose_updates.related_work: Gao, Ge, and Qian define the same uncentered endpoint \(L(\mathbf P)\) and prove their displayed balanced-sample plug-in rate. Comparisons here are restricted to the common fixed-\(d>4\), \(K\ge3\), balanced class. Their published class additionally covers all dimensions and \(K\ge2\); on the overlap the distributional class is the same arbitrary \(\mathcal P(\mathbb B_d)^K\), and their balanced i.i.d.-unit design induces the armwise product law used here. The improved theorem sharpens both the residual cap and active high-dimensional term on that overlap. Manole and Niles-Weed's two-margin theorem gives the closest all-estimator nonparametric lower architecture. The two-margin reduction embeds that published subclass inside the arbitrary-margin class, so its \(K^{-2}(m\log m)^{-2/d}\) lower bound transfers upward, but it does not close the logarithmic or arm-count gap. Hundrieser, Staudt, and Munk transfer entropy between two \(c\)-conjugate potentials; no cited theorem controls the aggregate of a growing jointly conjugate \(K\)-tuple. Ji, Lei, and Spector establish broad validity from dual feasibility, while Manole, Balakrishnan, and Wasserman study interval length for sliced Wasserstein distance; neither provides this arbitrary-margin one-sided expected-length converse. Generic discrete MOT complexity and hardness results do not preclude the fixed-dimensional squared-sum dynamic program proved here. The binary covariate-aware causal-transport papers remain informed-by comparators rather than extension targets. Mixability results for selected scalar or identical-margin classes do not settle arbitrary heterogeneous vector marginals. The STAR application comparison is conditional on the declared known-bound affine scale, i.i.d. superpopulation, complete randomization, and randomized balanced subsampling; the native unequal counts require a separate theorem.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The exact small-arm frontier \(K=o(N^{q_d})\) remains open. The current estimation sandwich has nonparametric lower term \(K^{-2}(m\log m)^{-2/d}\) and upper term \(K^{-1}m^{-2/d}\); the corresponding nonparametric ordered one-sided expected-length converse is not proved. The finite-support perturbation template has not been instantiated with endpoint separation, product-mixture total variation at most \(1/4\), and nonnegative reduced cost for every rematching column. Optimal-sum diameter does not by itself bound the aggregate sensitivity of all dual potentials, while fixed-dimensional orthogonal tensoring saturates. The certified algorithm is polynomial in \(N\) and \((K/\epsilon)^d\) only for fixed \(d\), and is not a generic polynomial-time exact MOT claim. Its corrected certificate uses only rational quantities \(h=1/\lceil32d/\epsilon\rceil\) and \(3dh\). The STAR audit discards observations, requires a known outcome bound and superpopulation model, and does not reproduce the native unequal-count tightening.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The proved contribution preserves \(L(\mathbf P)=K^{-2}\inf_\gamma\mathbb E_\gamma\|\sum_kZ_k\|_2^2\) as an uncentered second-moment endpoint. It assumes fixed \(d>4\), \(K\ge3\), balanced armwise product sampling, unit-ball support, and legal arrays with \(m=N/K\to\infty\), but no density or smoothness. Matching root-\(N\) bounds for estimation and uniformly honest one-sided expected excess length are claimed only when \(K\ge c_0N^{q_d}\), with \(q_5=1/6\) and \(q_d=1/4\) for \(d\ge6\). The explicit lower bound is the empirical-MOT plug-in rule calibrated by a uniform mean absolute-error allowance; no small-arm nonparametric length converse is claimed. For \(K=o(N^{q_d})\), exact rates, fixed-\(K\) logarithms, and the ordered lower family remain open. The finite-support construction is a search handle, not evidence that either a matching lower family or a sharper aggregate dual bound exists. The hypercube parity proposition remains a legal exact \(K=3,d=5\) benchmark with endpoint \(1/9\). Gao--Ge--Qian comparisons apply only on the common fixed-\(d>4\), \(K\ge3\), balanced overlap; their published class is broader in \(d\) and includes \(K=2\). The STAR audit applies only to its declared balanced randomized subsample and not the native \(161/37/36\) calculation.
